problem: Improve school quality through choice and competition.
title: Sweden introduces school vouchers and free choice of independent schools
context: Public schools were local monopolies and few private schools existed.
decision_made: Allow publicly funded independent schools and let families choose, with similar funding for both types.
action_taken: Reform took effect in 1992 and independent schools grew slowly.
observed_outcome: A main study found that a higher share of independent schools improved average results and long-run outcomes, mainly through competition effects, with gains appearing about a decade after the reform. Other studies of Swedish choice reforms found results from near zero to positive.
lessons: Effects of school choice can be slow, work through system-wide competition, and depend on how they are measured.
limitations: Only abstracts were read for competing studies. Results depend on the outcome measure, and effects are not the same as individual student gains.

claims.claim_text: The 1992 reform introduced vouchers and free choice between public and independent schools.
Böhlmark and Lindahl found that more independent-school students improved average performance, with effects appearing about a decade after the reform.
